title: Sequenced invocations: cross-tool result sanitation and loop-detection
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Summary: Implement a safe sequenced invocation loop that supports multi-tool chaining, preserves streaming semantics, enforces structured-output contracts, and prevents recursive result re-injection loops. This ticket covers design, runtime hooks, compatibility shims for existing function-calling contracts, and a lightweight runtime guardset (depth counts, result fingerprints, and circuit-breakers).

Motivation: Customer workloads increasingly chain 3-6 tools per request (extract -> transform -> external-call -> enrich -> format). We observed two classes of failures in internal and customer traces: 1) unbounded recursion where tool output is re-injected into a previous tool call and 2) corruption of the streaming frame when intermediate tools emit non-structured or non-stream-safe payloads. Both classes manifest as tail latency spikes and occasional SLO breaches.

Goals:
- Provide deterministic guards to detect and stop recursion or looped reinjection with clear diagnostic metadata.
- Ensure streaming responses keep correct chunk-level contracts when tools produce partial outputs (support passthrough + buffered fallback).
- Sanitize cross-tool results to be compatible with structured-output schemas before injection.
- Offer a compat-mode that preserves older behavior for flagged customers for one release cycle.

Non-goals: Rewriting tool APIs; full static verification of tool schemas (that is future work).

Deliverables:
- Runtime: invocation manager with per-request tool graph, depth counter, and fingerprint cache.
- Runtime: streaming adapter that can switch between passthrough and buffered-forwarding per-tool.
- SDK: additions to function-calling contract to declare stream-safety and output-schema hints.
- Console: per-request trace link, loop-detection reason, and suggested remediation.
- Tests: fuzzing harness for synthetic chaining with randomized outputs and end-to-end e2e tests with Dedicated clusters.
